commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: doctor

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Adding a project opens the operating system's folder dialog (see #werk-projects-add). On a machine where werk has no supported dialog, the Add project action does not fail silently. It shows that the dialog is not available, and says that starting werk in the project's folder adds the project (see #werk-projects-one-process). The git check and the offer to initialise a repository apply the same way on that path.

In tests the dialog is an external program, so a fake with a scripted folder path stands in for it, as for every external service (see #werk-test-external).

card werk-v0-conversations  [open]  PROPOSED — not in the map until it is accepted
In v0, a new conversation starts empty from a control in the tab strip, with the open card as its home card
why: The chat card says a person can keep more than one conversation, but the cards that define forking, parking and the tab strip are not decided. v0 needs one plain way to start a second conversation, so it starts an empty one and leaves the rest for later.

A person can keep more than one conversation (see #werk-chat). To make that possible without the undecided tab features, v0 gives the tab strip one control that starts a new conversation. The new conversation gets its own agent process (see #werk-chat-stdin) and an empty session. Its home card is the card open when it starts, and the home card is its tab label (see #werk-mc-split).

Each tab is a chip in the tab strip. A click on a chip switches the chat pane to that conversation and shows its newest message (see #werk-mc-tab-bottom). A tab whose agent died, or that has a running background agent, shows it as #werk-mc-live-dead and #werk-mc-bgagents say. Every conversation stays on the strip; v0 has no close, no park and no idle sweep.

---
card st-model-per-role  [decided]
Each pipeline agent runs on the model that its role needs
why: Most of the pipeline's cost comes from the agents that run many times per ticket: builder passes, reviewers and held-out runs. Opus stays where one mistake spreads to every later step or where a result is judged: the plan and the grader. The builder gets Sonnet with Opus as an advisor for the difficult parts, and the narrow or mechanical roles get Sonnet alone.

To keep cost down without weakening the gates, the pipeline picks the model of each agent from its role, not from one default.

+- The model of each pipeline agent comes from its role: the spec writer, the ticket writer and the grader run on Opus; the builder runs on Sonnet with Opus as advisor; the reviewers, the step author, the binder and the overseer classifiers run on Sonnet. The chat agent keeps the model of the chat selector. Models are pinned to exact ids, not aliases (#st-model-per-role, #opus-pin, #sonnet-pin, #werk-model-select).
- Every time limit — silence, classifier interval, wall clock, check timeout — is a parameter, clamped by one shared budget (#st-build-seam, #al-sample-budget).

- The builder loop, the merge loop, the held-out set and the overseer follow the cards cited in stories 83 to 102. The held-out set is built as its own slice, gated on the run's tree, before the merge loop runs it after each merge (#werk-heldout-before-merge).

- The server watches each build process it started and restarts a dead one as a fresh pass (#st-build-died). A Build press starts one detached process that plans and then runs the merge loop (#werk-board-build-subtree).
-- Each step's start, end, cost and, for a red step, its gate and cause are written to the project's pipeline log, which is the record the builder loop's tests read: see #werk-v0-pipeline-log.

+- Each step's start, end, cost and, for a red step, its gate and cause are written to the project's pipeline log, which is the record the builder loop's tests read: see #werk-v0-pipeline-log. A plan's start event lists its scope cards with tier and log position, and its end names a folder with its copy of the spec and the tickets it wrote. Transcripts and check output are files beside the log, not tracked by git (#ms-store-scope, #ms-store-plancopy, #ms-store-files, #ms-store-git).
### Checks, distribution and devex
- More than one conversation per project: tabs, forking a session, cross-tab recall, parking and the idle sweep, and tab keyboard shortcuts. #werk-multichat is postponed.
- An overseer for chat-pane and terminal sessions (#lp-overseer-scope).
- A limit on follow-up tickets per run (#st-build-run-cap).

+- Reports over the pipeline log: the fail report, the Measure view and its signal, column times, and the plan-turn cost of chat turns (#werk-v0-pipeline-log, #werk-cli-fails, #werk-write-measure-signal, #ms-col-time, #ms-store-plan).
+- Follow-up and escape records after a finished build (#ms-outcome-followup, #ms-outcome-escape, #werk-cli-followup).
+- Watching kill criteria: the scheduled check, the unmonitored state from a failed query, and the proposal from a fired criterion (#kill-trigger, #kill-fire). v0 records the criteria and shows them.
## Further Notes
- The prototype in its own repository is the bar. A v0 behaviour that differs from it is either a decided card the prototype never followed, or a gap to record as a card.

- The order of slices is the planner's choice, with three fixed points: the ticket checks come before the plan (#werk-ticket-check-verb); the held-out set comes before the merge loop runs it (#werk-heldout-before-merge); and the test harness with the fake agent comes before any slice that starts an agent.
- The kill criterion of #werk-base names the fallback: extend the prototype code.

-- Two decided cards name a mechanism that a later decided card replaced in part: #lp-stateless writes one record per pass to a per-run file, and #ms-store keeps one pipeline log per project; #werk-stack-api carries ids on the change signal, and #werk-write-changed sends a bare signal. v0 follows the later card in each pair.
+- #lp-stateless records each pass in the one pipeline log of #ms-store, and #werk-stack-api's change signal carries no ids, as #werk-write-changed says. The cards agree on both points.

- #werk-v0-pipeline-log is decided. #werk-v0-add-project-fallback still waits as a proposal. #werk-v0-conversations, also a proposal, gives a control for a second conversation, which the postponement of #werk-multichat rules out; this spec does not build it, and the proposal should be discarded.

- #werk-v0-seams names multichat in its browser coverage, and #werk-chat says a person can keep more than one conversation. Both point at #werk-multichat, which is postponed. v0 follows the postponement: one conversation per project.
